hints: Focus on what the yellow crystals test really means, recall the two groups that give a positive iodoform test.
List the C4 hydroxy-ketones that contain a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group, there are two different places to put the OH.
Now look for hydroxy-aldehydes that contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$ but are not methyl ketones, and add them to your count.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform condition**

Yellow crystals with alkaline $\text{I}_2$ is the tri-iodomethane test. It is positive for two structural features.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{ (methyl ketone) OR } \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \text{ (ethan-1-ol fragment)}$$

**Find the methyl ketone isomers**

We need $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ with $\text{C=O}$ plus $\text{OH}$. Start with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ which uses C1 and C2. The rest $\text{-R}$ must be $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}$ containing OH.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \text{ and } \text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$$
That is 1-hydroxybutan-2-one and 3-hydroxybutan-2-one. Both give a positive test because of the methyl ketone group. That is 2 so far.

**Find the hydroxy-aldehyde isomers with CH3CH(OH)**

Now consider aldehydes $\text{OHC}-$ with a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ fragment elsewhere. The only way to fit this in 4 carbons is:

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}$$
That is 3-hydroxybutanal. It is positive because of the secondary alcohol fragment, even though it is not a methyl ketone.

**Check the other isomers are negative and count**

Other hydroxy aldehydes like $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$ (2-hydroxybutanal), $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ (4-hydroxybutanal) and branched isomers do not contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so they are negative.

Total positive = 2 + 1 = 3.

options.A: 2 counts only the two hydroxy-ketones with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$. It misses the hydroxy-aldehyde $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}$ which is also positive via the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ route.
options.B: 3 is correct: $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$, and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}$. The first two are positive as methyl ketones, the third is positive as a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ alcohol.
options.C: 4 overcounts by including one extra isomer such as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$ (2-hydroxybutanal). That has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)}-$, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so it cannot form $\text{CHI}_3$.
options.D: 5 overcounts badly, likely by assuming every hydroxy aldehyde or ketone gives iodoform. Only structures with exactly $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ are positive.
